title: Whoever does the will (Matthew 12:22–50)
hookLine: found family is old news: his family at the door, and a circle that gets wider
tomorrow: why do some words stick with you and others just vanish?

lines: A GROUP CHAT CALLED THE FAM.
cards: A group chat named the fam, with nobody in it related by blood. A friend's mom who keeps a spare toothbrush for you. A holiday dinner made of roommates.
People build family out of friends all the time. Matthew has a scene where Jesus does something like it, on a long, hard day, with his own mother and brothers standing outside.

teach.b: The day has been sharp. He heals a man who was blind and couldn't speak, and some Pharisees say he drives out devils by Beelzebub.

teach.h: A TREE KNOWN BY ITS FRUIT.
teach.b: He answers with pictures, not anger: "every city or house divided against itself shall not stand," and "the tree is known by his fruit." Look at what the healing produced: a man who can see and speak.
Then a message passes through the packed room: your mother and your brothers are outside, wanting to speak with you. He answers with a question: "Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?"
He stretches out his hand toward his disciples.
"Behold my mother and my brethren! For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother."
Here's the detail to tell a friend: only his mother and brothers were at the door, but his answer adds a sister. The circle gets wider than the people who came.
Matthew never says whether he went out to them afterward, and nothing here pushes his family away.

Churches read the word brethren differently: some as Mary's later sons; Catholic and Orthodox Christians as close relatives such as cousins. Either way, family in this chapter is whoever does the will.

how: Some churches call their members brothers and sisters, and some Christians read Matthew 12:50 as the reason a congregation can feel like family to people far from their own.

games.q: a coworker has nowhere to go for the holidays. your family dinner is small and private. what fits Matthew 12:50?
o: send her a thoughtful card, so she knows you care.
ask your family about setting one more place.
keep it family-only; that's what holidays are for.
games.why: Jesus stretches out his hand toward people not related to him and says: behold my mother and my brethren. a table can be wider than blood.

practice: Bring to mind one friend who has been family to you, someone who showed up when it counted. Write them a short text in your head: one specific thank-you, a time and a place.
Hold the words while you breathe; whether you send them is up to you.

wordCard.voice: Whoever does the will. Jesus' answer to a knock at the door: his family is wider than the ones outside.

orig.note: Greek for will, the word in Matthew 12:50: whoever does the will of my Father.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: my brother and sister, said of people with no blood in common. Rest easy.
